FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.86  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` can terminate the FSM on the basis of malformed or adversarial `findings` that are not tied to successful responses.** The method runs failure detection over `responses`, but then unconditionally feeds the separate caller-supplied `findings` list into convergence detection and diminishing-returns logic. There is no gating that findings must come from models with non-failing responses, from active models, or even from any response at all. As a result, a round can contain an EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED response for a model while still accepting that same model’s `Finding`s and using them to raise `kappa`, increase yield, or trigger severity vetoes. This is deeper than the already-noted “caller trust” issue: it is a cross-area integrity break where Area 6 failure classification and Areas 4–5 evidence ingestion can directly contradict each other within the same round.  
PROPOSED_FIX: derive accepted findings from validated responses only, or explicitly filter findings after failure detection to include only active models with semantically successful responses; reject mixed states where a failed response contributes findings.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.82  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` is not idempotent and double-processing the same round corrupts multiple subsystems.** A repeated call with the same `round_idx` appends another `RoundResult`, appends another underperformance sample to `_perf_history`, appends another role-assignment failure bit, overwrites convergence data for that round, and may update live fingerprints again from the same evidence. Because `_round_results` is append-only while convergence state for a round is overwriteable, the manager can end up with inconsistent histories across areas from one duplicate delivery/retry. This is a cross-cutting orchestration flaw distinct from the previously reported overwrite-in-convergence issue: here the full manager lacks any processed-round guard or deduplication contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: make `process_round()` reject already-processed round indices, or require a unique round/attempt token and enforce idempotent updates across all subsystems.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.78  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` can accept and persist a logically impossible round after the PM has already been excluded by non-ABORT recovery.** In `FailureHandler.get_recovery()`, PM receives special handling only for EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED; repeated FORMAT or UNDERPERFORM failures fall through the standard policy and can yield `RETRY_CLARIFIED`, `DEGRADE`, `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, etc. Meanwhile `should_abort()` only checks whether the PM model ID is absent from `_active_models`, and PM is removed from `_active_models` only on `EXCLUDE`. That means the PM can repeatedly fail in ways that imply unusable management behavior while remaining active and the run continues. This is not the same as the already-reported inert recovery-action problem: it is a PM-specific violation of the claimed “PM abort” safety invariant across Area 6 and orchestration.  
PROPOSED_FIX: define PM policy for all failure types explicitly; either any PM semantic failure is terminal, or PM-specific non-terminal recoveries must be implemented and enforced consistently.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.80  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`update_fingerprints()` silently skips excluded models, so a model excluded during the current round never has its latest observed behavior recorded.** `process_round()` performs failure handling before fingerprint updates, and `update_fingerprints()` iterates only over `self.failure_handler.active_models`. If a model produced a valid response and findings this round but was excluded during failure handling for another failure type or policy decision, its round evidence is discarded from adaptive capability state. That creates an asymmetry: included models learn from the round, excluded ones do not, even though exclusion may itself have been based on stale or partial state. This is a cross-area ordering bug affecting failure handling and adaptive routing.  
PROPOSED_FIX: update fingerprints for all models that participated in the round, then apply active/inactive status to future allocation only; or separately store last-observed metrics even for excluded models.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Unknown models can permanently contaminate failure state and role-history state without ever belonging to the managed pool.** `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` and `get_recovery()` both use `setdefault()` on unknown `model_id`s, creating `_perf_history` and `_failure_history` entries for arbitrary IDs. `RoleAssignment.record_failure()` does the same for `_failure_history`. Because `process_round()` iterates caller-provided response keys, a bogus model ID can create persistent internal state and appear in downstream diagnostics, even though it will never be allocatable or part of `self.models`. This is broader than simple “unknown input accepted”: it is silent state expansion across multiple subsystems.  
PROPOSED_FIX: enforce membership validation at the `DynamicManager` boundary and reject or quarantine unknown IDs before passing data into any subsystem.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.74  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The event protocol can report a round as “complete” before it is known whether processing will abort with failure, converge, or stop, and then report “complete” again for fingerprint updates.** This is more than naming confusion: external observers can receive a semantically final-sounding progress event before any key decisions are made, and may act on stale assumptions. Because `process_round()` emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` at entry and `update_fingerprints()` emits another `ROUND_COMPLETE`, downstream control planes cannot infer a reliable lifecycle from the public API. The problem spans orchestration, monitoring, and failure handling semantics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: introduce distinct events such as `ROUND_PROCESSING_START`, `ROUND_DECISIONS_MADE`, and `FINGERPRINTS_UPDATED`, reserving `ROUND_COMPLETE` for the true terminal point of round processing.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.71  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Negative or nonsensical round economics can invert the diminishing-returns logic and make harmful rounds look beneficial.** `process_round()` accepts arbitrary `round_cost` and forwards it into `DiminishingReturnsDetector` with no validation. If `round_cost < 0`, then positive `delta_y` yields negative `mu`, making the system appear to be in diminishing returns immediately; conversely negative `delta_y` with negative cost yields positive `mu`. This is not covered by earlier generic numeric-validation findings because it is a specific cross-area control bug: an invalid economic input can directly drive FSM termination.  
PROPOSED_FIX: enforce `round_cost >= 0` at the API boundary and reject non-finite costs.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.69  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` makes class IDs unstable across recomputation in a way that can silently invalidate external references or caches.** `class_id` is assigned as `ec_{idx}` based on iteration order of `clusters.items()`, which depends on union-find root selection and input ordering. Since cumulative classes are recomputed from scratch after each round, the same semantic class can receive different IDs over time even if its member set only grows. This is deeper than mere reporting instability: any downstream component or audit tool that stores class IDs as persistent identities will be broken.  
PROPOSED_FIX: derive class IDs from stable content, e.g. sorted member finding IDs hash or canonical representative selection.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION: 0.72  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`pairwise_joint_failure()` violates its own docstring/model for self-pairs and permits impossible semantics through `set_vulnerability(model_i, model_i, v)`.** `get_vulnerability(i, i)` hardcodes `1.0`, but `set_vulnerability()` also stores a `frozenset({i})` entry for self-vulnerability without rejection. That stored value is then ignored by `get_vulnerability`, creating a silent write-only state. More importantly, allowing self-pairs in the API suggests a meaningful self-correlation concept even though the implementation treats self-failure as certainty of shared vulnerability. This is an unreported contract inconsistency in the correlated-failure model.  
PROPOSED_FIX: reject `model_i == model_j` in `set_vulnerability()` and document self-pair semantics explicitly.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.66  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits no event for UNDERPERFORM even though `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` exists.** Prior findings covered missing/incorrect event typing for FORMAT and missing event emission in some branches, but the underperformance path remains silently unobservable to the event interface despite being a first-class failure type and an important driver of role downgrades. This leaves monitoring blind to the only sustained-performance failure mode.  
PROPOSED_FIX: emit `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` when the persistence predicate triggers, including recent performance window details in metadata.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.64  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager` has no invariant check that the locked PM remains in `RoleAssignment.role_map` after reassignment, despite relying on that assumption in several areas.** `RoleAssignment.reassign()` always seeds `new_map` with `pm_model_id`, but if external mutation or earlier corruption removes or renames that PM ID, `FailureHandler.should_abort()`, allocation admissibility, and event interpretation all degrade inconsistently. Given that public mutable dicts are shared across components, the absence of a central invariant check is a real orchestration risk, not just a style issue.  
PROPOSED_FIX: after every reassignment and before every public operation, assert that exactly one PM exists and its ID equals `pm_model_id` and belongs to the active or known model set.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.61  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`update_fingerprints()` can drive capability values outside their intended semantic range if prior state is already invalid, because there is no post-update clamping or finite check.** Observations are mostly in `[0,1]`, but `old_fp` values come from unvalidated `ModelSpec.fingerprint` inputs. EMA then propagates NaN, inf, negatives, or values >1 into live state, which subsequently affects role scoring and monitoring. This is distinct from earlier generic NaN-acceptance notes because the adaptive loop amplifies and persists the bad state round after round.  
PROPOSED_FIX: validate `CapabilityFingerprint` fields on construction and clamp/check finiteness after each EMA update before storing to `_live_fingerprints`.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.58  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The manager’s public API conflates “round” and “phase” in a way that makes cross-round analytics structurally ambiguous.** BLIND, SYNTH, and iterative rounds all flow through the same `process_round()` signature and are stored in the same `RoundResult` shape, but tasks, costs, findings, and stop/convergence semantics differ materially across phases. Even aside from the already-found duplicated round index bug, the data model itself does not distinguish what kind of processing a record represents. This makes any downstream analysis of cost/yield or model performance phase-sensitive but impossible to do correctly from stored results alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: add an explicit phase field to `RoundResult` and phase-aware processing paths, or separate synthesis results from numbered round results entirely.

FINDING_ID: ROUND6_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.55  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ModelSpec`, `Task`, `Finding`, and `ModelResponse` have no local invariant enforcement despite comments claiming bounded domains, so impossible values can be created long before config validation ever runs.** For example, `Task.criticality`, `Finding.severity`, `Finding.abstraction_index`, and `CapabilityFingerprint` fields are all documented as bounded but are plain dataclass fields. This is not just a generic validation complaint: multiple algorithms assume these ranges algebraically for probability-like scores, EMA, convergence, and weighted sums, so the lack of object-level invariants is a systemic design hole.  
PROPOSED_FIX: add `__post_init__` validation to core dataclasses for finiteness and documented bounds, not just to config.
